description: Standup reads your git commits and your agents' sessions and writes the end-of-day update you can no longer write from memory.

ui.aboutDescription: What {site} reads, what it writes and who made it.
ui.notFoundBody: This page does not exist. No commit made it, yours or an agent’s.
ui.aboutBody: {site} is a free plugin for coding agents. Ask it for your standup update and it writes one for a day, a week or a month. Radu Ceuca built it at What Could Go Wrong to answer one question at the end of the day: what did I do.
ui.aboutPrivacy: This website uses Microsoft Clarity to see how its pages are used. It sets a cookie only if you said yes. The plugin is separate: its scripts open no network connection.
ui.consentBody: {site} remembers what you did all day. May this website remember you were here? It takes a Microsoft Clarity cookie. Say no and it still sees how the page is used, then forgets you.
ui.headline: You and your agents were busy all day.
ui.lede00: It’s {time}, you should be asleep and two agents are still going. You told yourself you would stop at eleven. Go to bed: Standup reads the night’s work when you wake up and tells you what they did while you slept.
ui.lede01: It’s {time}, and “one more prompt” was an hour ago. The house is quiet and you are the only light on in the street. Close the laptop: Standup will know in the morning what that last prompt turned into.
ui.lede02: It’s {time}, an idea woke you up and you started a session from your phone, in bed, in the dark, so you would not lose it. By breakfast you will not be sure it happened. Standup will remind you that it did, and show you what came of it.
ui.lede03: It’s {time}, nobody in the house is awake and three agents are. They are doing the work you used to stay up for, and they do not need you watching. Standup keeps the record, so you can keep sleeping.
ui.lede04: It’s {time}, and the agents finished a while ago with nobody there to see it. Hours of work, done, and no one to say well done to. Standup reads what they left behind when you get up, and gives you the credit.
ui.lede05: It’s {time}, your alarm has not gone off and a pull request has already been opened in your name. You have shipped something today and you have not opened your eyes. Standup tells you what it was, over coffee.
ui.lede06: It’s {time}, you are awake before the alarm and already reaching for your phone to see what finished overnight. This used to be the quiet hour. Standup has the answer in six lines, so you can put the phone down and have the quiet back.
ui.lede07: It’s {time}, the coffee is brewing, somebody small needs breakfast, and the laptop is open “just to check”. You are in two places and fully in neither. Standup does the checking and reads the night back to you, so you can be at the table.
ui.lede08: It’s {time}, the team standup is in an hour and yesterday is a blur. You know you worked. You could not say on what. Standup reads yesterday back to you, your commits and your agents’, before the coffee is done.
ui.lede09: It’s {time}, the standup has started and somebody just said “you go first”. Everyone is looking at you, and your mind has gone to that white, empty place. Standup already wrote yours, so read it out and breathe.
ui.lede10: It’s {time}, you opened four Claude Code sessions before your first meeting and have already lost track of which one is doing what. It is not even lunch and the day is getting away from you. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work so far and tells you where the day stands.
ui.lede11: It’s {time}, you are in a meeting that could have been an email, nodding, while behind this window three agents are doing your actual job. You will walk out with no idea what they did. Standup will tell you the moment the meeting lets you go.
ui.lede12: It’s {time}, you are eating lunch at your desk and approving permission prompts with a fork in your other hand. You have not tasted any of it. Standup counts what the morning shipped, so for twenty minutes lunch can just be lunch.
ui.lede13: It’s {time}, you are back from lunch to three finished sessions and one that asked you a question fifty minutes ago and has been waiting politely ever since. You feel behind on work you did not do. Standup sorts out what got done while you were away.
ui.lede14: It’s {time}, and a branch you do not remember creating has six commits on it. They look fine, which is somehow worse. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work and writes down what has shipped so far, including the parts you were not there for.
ui.lede15: It’s {time}, the afternoon has gone soft and you just approved a diff you could not describe to a colleague if they asked. You are a little ashamed of that. Standup can describe it: it reads what went in today and says so plainly.
ui.lede16: It’s {time}, and somebody wants a status by end of day, which is now a real time and not far off. You have worked all day and cannot name three things you did. Standup writes the status from what you and your agents did, not from what you remember.
ui.lede17: It’s {time}, the day is officially over and your manager has sent “quick update?” with nothing after it. Your stomach does the small drop it always does. Standup writes the reply, and it turns out you did more than you thought.
ui.lede18: It’s {time}, you have a dozen Claude Code sessions mid-flight, a handful of branches and no clear memory of the morning. How did we get here? Did we get anything done today? You need to pick up your kid from acting classes in 1h. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work and writes the summary for you, so you can go.
ui.lede19: It’s {time}, dinner is on the table, the laptop is shut, and one agent is still running in a worktree you forgot about. Someone is telling you about their day and you are half listening for a fan. Let it run: Standup will find it, and tell you tomorrow what it did.
ui.lede20: It’s {time}, the kid is asleep at last and you have opened the laptop for ten minutes, just to see where things are. You promised yourself you would not. Standup shows you where the day ended in six lines, which is all you came for.
ui.lede21: It’s {time}, and the ten minutes were an hour ago. The tea next to you has gone cold twice. Standup writes today’s update now, while there is still a today to write about, and then you can stop.
ui.lede22: It’s {time}, and you are telling yourself you will write the update first thing tomorrow, when you are fresh. You will not be fresh, and you will not remember any of this. Standup will.
ui.lede23: It’s {time}, you are brushing your teeth and thinking about a branch. The day will not leave you alone until somebody writes it down. Standup has, so let it go: the branch will still be there in the morning.
ui.installNote: Its scripts read files on your own disk and open no network connection.
ui.receiptCaption: The numbers behind it, printed by the Alibi 3000
ui.readsBody: Standup gives you four to six lines you can say out loud. Paste them into Slack, say them at standup, or keep them as proof the day happened.
ui.weekTitle: On Friday, ask for the week.
ui.weekBody: A week is covered Monday to Sunday, day by day, and a month the same way, so Monday’s work is still there on Friday.
ui.numbersTitle: It also says what the agents cost.
ui.numbersBody: The dollar figure is an estimate at API list prices. On a subscription you pay none of it per token, and it is still worth knowing before someone else asks.
ui.requirements: Needs Python 3.9 or later and git. Runs on macOS and Linux.
ui.askTitle: "What did you work on today?" is a hard question now.
ui.askBody: You start three things before lunch, an agent finishes two of them, and another runs in a worktree you forgot about.
ui.agentsTitle: It reads git and eight agents.
ui.agentPromptLabel: Or have your agent install it
ui.agentPrompt: Read {llms} to learn what Standup reads and how to install it. Run the install command it lists for the agent you are. When it is installed, write my standup update for today and show me the report.
ui.exampleTitle: This is Tuesday 17 November 2026, a day spent on this page. And the week before, and the month.
ui.updateCaption: The update, as it pastes into Slack with markup on
ui.noteStatus: 🔁 marks a merge, ✅ work finished here and 🚧 work still in progress, so nobody reads a merge as new work.
ui.noteCache: 99% of the tokens are cache reads, billed at a twentieth of the input price or less.
ui.noteCost: An estimate at Anthropic’s list prices. A model with no listed price is counted and marked unpriced.
ui.closeBody: The update is written. The agents will keep going without you, and tomorrow Standup tells you what they did.
ui.voiceNote: A voice rewords each line. Names, numbers and status marks stay as they are.
ui.sourcesNote: What shipped comes from git, whoever wrote it. Cursor and Antigravity keep no token counts on disk, so only their sessions are counted.
ui.installCursor: Then turn Standup on under Plugins in Cursor, and say “write my standup update”.
ui.installCopy: This clones the repository and copies the skill into the folder your agent reads. Then say “write my standup update”.

ui.claudeTitle: Daily standup plugin for Claude Code
ui.claudeDescription: {site} reads your Claude Code transcripts and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens and an estimated cost for every session.
ui.claudeBody: {site} reads the transcripts Claude Code keeps in ~/.claude/projects, and your git history, and writes what you and your sessions did today. Tokens are counted per folder, branch and day, with an estimated cost at Anthropic's list prices. Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days, so a report reaches back that far unless you raise cleanupPeriodDays.
ui.codexDescription: {site} reads your Codex sessions and your git commits and writes the day's update, with the tokens Codex used in each folder.
ui.codexBody: {site} reads the sessions Codex keeps in ~/.codex, and your git history, and writes what you and Codex did today. Codex records no branch, so its tokens are counted per folder and day. OpenAI's models have no built-in price: the report counts their tokens and marks the cost unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.cursorDescription: {site} writes the day's update from every commit you and Cursor made, and counts your Cursor sessions. Cursor keeps no token counts on disk.
ui.cursorBody: Cursor keeps no token counts on disk, so {site} counts its sessions and takes the rest from git: every commit you and Cursor made today, on every branch. On a day spent in Cursor the token totals are lower than the truth. What shipped is complete either way.
ui.geminiTitle: Daily standup extension for Gemini CLI
ui.geminiDescription: {site} installs as a Gemini CLI extension. It reads your Gemini sessions and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens per folder.
ui.geminiBody: {site} installs as a Gemini CLI extension. It reads the sessions Gemini CLI keeps in ~/.gemini, and your git history, and writes what you and Gemini did today. Tokens are counted per folder and day. Google's models have no built-in price: the report counts their tokens and marks the cost unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.grokDescription: {site} reads your Grok sessions and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens wherever Grok's log records them.
ui.grokBody: {site} reads Grok's sessions and its usage log in ~/.grok, and your git history, and writes what you and Grok did today. Recent Grok versions may not write usage records; the setup check says whether yours does. xAI's models have no built-in price: the report counts their tokens and marks the cost unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.opencodeDescription: {site} is a skill you copy into opencode. It reads opencode's database and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens.
ui.opencodeBody: opencode has no plugin route for skills, so {site} is one skill folder you copy in. It reads opencode's database in ~/.local/share/opencode, and your git history, and writes what you and opencode did today. Claude models are priced out of the box. Any other provider's tokens are counted and marked unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.llmsAbout: {site} is a free, MIT-licensed plugin for coding agents. It is one skill, standup: it writes the update for a day, a week, a month or any date range. It reads git history and the session files your agents keep on disk, and opens no network connection.
ui.llmsInstall: To install it, run the command for the agent you are. Then use the standup skill for today.

ui.llmsReadmeNote: what each agent gives, configuration, pricing and what leaves your machine
ui.llmsSkillNote: the instructions your agent follows when it runs the skill
